business_ops.seasonality: The dairy industry has two distinct seasons: the winter flush season, when milk supply is abundant, and the summer season, when supply drops by a relative 20% to 30% depending on the region and monsoon conditions (Source: 1Lattice Report). North India faces higher fluctuation in milk availability than South India on account of extreme summer and winter temperatures. The Company runs a milk balancing system: during the winter flush it converts excess milk into high-shelf-life products — cheddar cheese (10 to 12 month ripening period), UHT long-shelf life products (6 to 9 month shelf life) and high heat powder for internal use in ice cream — and during summer it shifts to high-demand products such as ice cream, beverages, curd and buttermilk. Demand does not always align with seasonal supply (for example demand peaks around certain holidays regardless of raw milk production levels).

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Integrated farm-to-retail model. BACKWARD: raw milk — the primary raw material — is sourced predominantly direct from farmers with no formal supply arrangements. As of March 31, 2026 the Company procured from 74,654 farmers (of whom 33,126 were women) across 25 districts of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Maharashtra, all within a 400 kilometre radius of Perundurai (67,615 farmers in Fiscal 2025; 67,807 in Fiscal 2024). Total raw milk procurement was 396.15, 307.20 and 272.80 million litres in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, of which 294.48 million litres (74.34%), 261.59 million litres (85.15%) and 263.55 million litres (96.61%) came directly from dairy farmers and 101.67 million litres (25.66%), 45.61 million litres (14.85%) and 9.25 million litres (3.39%) from third party dairy operators — the direct-from-farmer share has fallen sharply over the three years. Procurement is geographically concentrated in Tamil Nadu at 374.40 million litres (94.51%), 300.08 million litres (97.68%) and 271.77 million litres (99.62%); 'Others' (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh) was 21.75 million litres (5.49%), 7.12 million litres (2.32%) and 1.03 million litres (0.38%). Farmers are paid directly every 7 to 10 days, with middlemen eliminated; support includes cattle feed, silage training, fodder seeds, veterinary support, vaccinations, artificial insemination and cattle-loan facilitation, with 8, 10 and 28 farmer training programmes in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. A three-tier quality structure runs from 3,907 AMCUs (3 parameters) to 29 chilling centres comprising Milk Chilling Centres and Bulk Milk Coolers (21 parameters, located within a 30 to 40 kilometre radius of collection villages) to the Perundurai Manufacturing Facility (31 parameters). Realisation per litre of milk procured was approximately ₹77.79 in Fiscal 2026, stated to be the highest among listed peers (Source: 1Lattice Report). FORWARD: the Company operates its own logistics — as of March 31, 2026, 63 milk vans/tankers (average capacity 23,150 litres; 44 in Fiscal 2025 and 34 in Fiscal 2024), 282 reefer trucks with in-built refrigeration (payload approximately 10,485 kilograms; 252 in Fiscal 2025, 201 in Fiscal 2024) and 34 ambient trucks (payload approximately 24,350 kilograms; 21 in Fiscal 2025, 34 in Fiscal 2024), of which 26 owned vehicles are electric; IoT-enabled real-time fleet tracking and route optimisation, with return-load optimisation carrying third-party goods such as apples, cocoa powder, sweet corn, rice and butter. Stated to be the only dairy-focused company among its listed peers with entirely in-house logistics and manufacturing (Source: 1Lattice Report). Downstream cold chain at retail: 15,062 visi coolers, 25,824 ice cream freezers and 573 chocolate coolers deployed as of March 31, 2026, with a plan to deploy 30,000 ice cream freezers, 24,000 visi coolers and 12,000 chocolate coolers across Fiscals 2026, 2027 and 2028 funded partly from the Net Proceeds. Advertisement and business promotion expenses were ₹796.12 million (2.54% of revenue from operations), ₹711.32 million (3.03%) and ₹205.60 million (1.13%) in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. FURTHER FORWARD INTEGRATION PLANNED from the Net Proceeds: whey protein concentrate capacity of 10 tons per day and edible/pharma-grade lactose capacity of 44 tons per day (moving whey powder up the value chain from a bulk commodity), a dedicated 60 TPD yogurt plant with packing lines rated at 50,800 containers per hour, a fresh cheese line for feta and gouda, processed-cheese capacity addition with a continuous cooker, and a dedicated warehouse for cold and dry products within the Perundurai facility.

market_position.basis: Value-added dairy products company (paneer, cheese, curd, butter, ghee, yogurt, ice cream, UHT, plus frozen/RTE/RTC and chocolates) operating exclusively in value-added dairy rather than liquid milk, from a single USFDA-approved facility at Perundurai, Erode, Tamil Nadu, selling across 22 states and 5 union territories. Stated FY26 market shares (Source: 1Lattice Report): organised packaged paneer in India ~19.0% (largest private brand); organised cheese in South India ~12% (largest private brand) and ~5% nationally among private players (ranked third); organised curd in South India ~7%; organised yogurt in India ~13% (among the top two private brands); organised Greek yogurt in India 35-40%. The RHP states the company is the fastest growing packaged food company in India among companies with revenue above ₹15,000 million, at a 31.26% revenue CAGR from Fiscal 2024 to Fiscal 2026. overview.business_model: The Company buys raw milk direct from farmers (74,654 farmers across 25 districts within a 400 kilometre radius of its plant, supplemented by third party dairy operators), chills it through 3,907 automated milk collection units and 29 chilling centres, and processes it at one owned facility at Perundurai into premium value-added dairy products rather than liquid milk. It sells 22 product categories and 640 SKUs through general trade (37.69% of Fiscal 2026 revenue from operations), modern trade (23.07%), HoReCa (16.70%), e-commerce (13.70%), bulk B2B sales (8.07%) and its own parlours/online platform (0.77%), reaching more than 3,75,000 retail touchpoints through 4,001 distributors and 57 C&F depots, with its own reefer/ambient truck fleet and 15,062 visi coolers, 25,824 ice cream freezers and 573 chocolate coolers placed at retail. Revenue from operations was ₹31,383.64 million in Fiscal 2026 (₹23,495.03 million in Fiscal 2025; ₹18,216.09 million in Fiscal 2024), a 31.26% CAGR, with gross profit margin 32.97%, EBITDA margin 13.87% and PAT of ₹1,270.09 million (PAT margin 4.05%) in Fiscal 2026. Premium pricing (paneer and curd typically 10% to 30% above the average market price of large Indian brands) drives realisation of approximately ₹77.79 per litre of milk procured.

employee_strength.note: 1,317 permanent employees as of March 31, 2026, comprising plant and office 534, sales and marketing 512, quality control 30 and milk collection centres 241. Headcount has fallen over the period — 1,317 (Fiscal 2026) from 1,524 (Fiscal 2025) and 1,694 (Fiscal 2024) — with 398, 547 and 671 resignations and attrition rates of 29.08%, 34.05% and 41.13% respectively. In addition, 3,224 contract labourers were engaged as of March 31, 2026. There are no recognised trade unions and no material work stoppages in the last three Fiscals.

genesis.founding_story: The business began in 1998 as the partnership firm M.M.D. Dairy at Erode, Tamil Nadu, founded by the promoters Sathishkumar T and Anitha S, who were both associated with the firm as partners. Paneer production commenced in 1998, and the Company was one of the first private companies to launch branded packaged paneer in India, subsequently establishing categories in curd, ghee, butter, cheese, yogurt, ice cream, UHT long-shelf life products, chocolates and sweetened condensed milk. The firm was renamed Milky Mist Dairy Food in 2006, converted into a private limited company in 2014, and converted into a public limited company in May 2025. Sathishkumar T (Chairman and Managing Director) has over 27 years of experience in the dairy and food industry and Anitha S (Whole-time Director) over 24 years; Dr. K Rathnam (Whole-time Director and CEO) has over 34 years in the food products sector, having been a senior manager (quality assurance) at Heinz India Private Limited and managing director at Kaira District Co-operative Milk Producers' Union Limited.

internal_operational.detail: Manufacturing operations depend on large volumes of raw milk, the majority procured from Tamil Nadu. The Company procures the majority of milk directly from dairy farmers with whom it has no formal arrangements, and from third party dairy operators primarily on a purchase order basis, so suppliers are not obligated to supply and may sell to competitors. Availability and price are subject to seasonal, environmental, cattle-health and government-policy factors. A decentralised procurement model has been initiated with sourcing from Maharashtra. Social, political or economic disruption, natural calamities, civil unrest, dairy farmers' protests, cattle disease outbreaks or state/local policy changes could substantially affect procurement; a livestock disease outbreak could reduce volume and quality, trigger closure of collection routes, chilling centres or the manufacturing facility in containment zones, disrupt farmer arrangements and erode consumer confidence.

strategy_growth.detail: The Net Proceeds are intended for repayment or prepayment of borrowings, capital expenditure for the expansion and modernisation of the Perundurai Manufacturing Facility, deployment of visi coolers, ice-cream freezers and chocolate coolers, and general corporate purposes. Other than certain purchase orders, no definitive agreements have been entered into with vendors, and cost estimates rely on the ITCOT Report prepared from vendor quotations valid for limited periods, some denominated in currencies other than the Indian Rupee. Completion depends on external agencies responsible for civil and structural works, installation and commissioning of machinery and supply and testing of equipment. The expansion requires various approvals at appropriate stages. The Company also intends to install and commission lines to manufacture whey protein concentrate and lactose, products in which it has no prior manufacturing experience.
strategy_growth.evidence: Purchase orders placed with SPX Flow Technology India Private Limited and KOURTOGLOU S.A. - Alfa Machine aggregating Rs 897.49 million, approximately 17.33% of the total estimated capital expenditure cost for the expansion and modernisation of the Perundurai Manufacturing Facility, of which payments aggregating Rs 487.02 million had been made as on June 30, 2026 (Rs 280.45 million from internal accruals and Rs 206.57 million from the proceeds of the Pre-IPO Placement). Cost estimates rely on the ITCOT Report dated July 2026 issued by ITCOT Limited; foreign currency quotations converted at the RBI reference rate as of May 29, 2026.
strategy_growth.title: No definitive arrangements for utilising certain portions of the Net Proceeds; costs based on quotations and management estimates

strategy_growth.detail: Growth strategies include strengthening the position in Southern India and establishing a stronger presence in other regions, expanding production capacity and augmenting procurement capabilities, further strengthening brand visibility and brand equity, growing inorganically through strategic acquisitions and leveraging technology to improve operational and cost efficiency. Expansion into semi-urban and rural regions faces infrastructure and distribution limitations, logistical challenges, lower consumer awareness, competition from local players, and regulatory and environmental constraints, with price-conscious consumers in those regions.
strategy_growth.evidence: Revenue from operations Rs 31,383.64 / 23,495.03 / 18,216.09 million with year-on-year growth of 33.58%, 28.98% and 30.66% in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Profit for the year Rs 1,270.09 / 460.74 / 194.44 million with PAT margin 4.05%, 1.96% and 1.07%. In Fiscal 2025 the average procurement price decreased by 0.95% compared with Fiscal 2024, and profit increased by 136.96% from Fiscal 2024 to Fiscal 2025. Profit increased by 175.66% from Fiscal 2025 to Fiscal 2026, on account of improved operating leverage and cost efficiencies reducing total expenses as a percentage of revenue from operations from 96.50% to 95.16%, and recognition of previously unrecognised MAT credit of Rs 245.61 million pertaining to earlier years.
strategy_growth.title: Inability to effectively manage growth or implement growth strategies

strategy_growth.detail: Products are sold under the umbrella brand 'Milky Mist' and sub-brands 'SmartChef', 'Capella' and 'Misty Lite', with recently acquired brands 'Briyas' and 'Asal'. Brand development depends on public perception and recognition of product quality, and negative publicity about healthfulness, safety or quality could discourage consumers. Increased advertising and marketing spend may not translate into increased sales or revenue. Deployment of visi coolers, ice cream freezers and chocolate coolers entails capital expenditure that may not translate into proportional revenues, and because these units are booked as depreciable assets, delay in deployment still incurs depreciation expense.
strategy_growth.evidence: Advertisement and business promotion expenses Rs 796.12 million (2.54% of revenue from operations) in Fiscal 2026, Rs 711.32 million (3.03%) in Fiscal 2025 and Rs 205.60 million (1.13%) in Fiscal 2024. Visi coolers, ice cream freezers and chocolate coolers deployed in 13,211, 4,065 and 10,503 retail outlets as of March 31, 2026, 2025 and 2024. As on March 31, 2026, 15,062 visi coolers, 25,824 ice cream freezers and 573 chocolate coolers deployed. Visi cooler deployment began in Fiscal 2011.
strategy_growth.title: Significant and continuing expenditure on brand visibility and brand equity, and on deployment of coolers and freezers

concerns_observed: The equity base is very small relative to the debt and the asset base it carries: net worth Rs 3,779.95 mn and NAV Rs 5.87 per share at March 31, 2026, against total borrowings of Rs 16,718.53 mn (from Rs 13,763.76 mn and Rs 10,367.23 mn), debt to equity 3.61 times, fund-based outstanding borrowings of Rs 13,907.23 mn as on May 31, 2026, and personal guarantees from the two Promoters aggregating Rs 13,844.53 mn as on May 31, 2026. A trademark assigned by the Promoter to the Company is hypothecated to lenders; the Company states it is currently marketing under a new, unhypothecated logo.

Capacity was multiplied and then ran empty in the same year: paneer installed capacity was raised from 72 to 192 MT per day in Fiscal 2026 and utilisation fell from 110.49% (FY25) to 52.44% (FY26) - against 89.47% in FY24. Set curd ran at 23.25%, chocolate 4.43% (production fell from 383 MT to 178 MT), sweetened condensed milk 11.76%, ice cream 29.40%, ghee 48.75% (from 71.76% after doubling to 48 MT/day), whey powder 48.93%, batter 22.48% (from 94.16%) and parotta 42.15% (from 86.35%) - all on available, not installed, capacity.

Against that utilisation record, Rs 3,945.00 mn of Net Proceeds funds further NEW product lines - whey protein concentrate 10 TPD and lactose 44 TPD (products the RHP states the Company has no prior manufacturing experience in), a 60 TPD yogurt plant with packing lines rated at 50,800 containers per hour, feta and gouda, and processed-cheese additions - while cheddar cheese capacity is separately being taken from 15.6 to 120 MT per day.

Execution rests almost entirely on quotations: purchase orders have been placed with only two vendors, SPX Flow Technology India and KOURTOGLOU S.A. - Alfa Machine, aggregating Rs 897.49 mn, approximately 17.33% of the capex object's estimated cost, of which Rs 487.02 mn had been paid as on June 30, 2026. The RHP states expressly 'Other than this, we have not entered into any definitive agreements with any of the other vendors', with quotations expiring between December 31, 2026 and June 5, 2027, foreign-currency prices struck at the RBI reference rate of May 29, 2026, truck quotations described as indicative, and the funding requirement not appraised by any bank, financial institution or independent agency.

Adverse audit remarks run across BOTH the Company and the Subsidiary and across all three Fiscals: PPE physical verification reconciled only to approximately 97% of gross block at the Company (balance 3% pending at FY26 year end) and to approximately 79% at the Subsidiary (approximately 21% not reconciled); the Subsidiary's FY2025 inventories could not be commented on 'in the absence of inventory records'; audit-trail (edit log) gaps at the Company for FY2024 and until December 14, 2024 / September 12, 2024 for customer, vendor and price masters, and at the Subsidiary through FY2024, FY2025 and until August 15 / October 13, 2025; internal audit coverage and timeliness 'requires improvement' in FY2026.

Stock statements filed with the consortium banks did not agree with the books in two successive fourth quarters: inventory Rs 3,160.10 mn per quarterly returns against Rs 3,424.68 mn per books for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 (difference Rs 264.50 mn), and Rs 2,383.16 mn against Rs 2,608.17 mn for the quarter ended March 31, 2025 (difference Rs 225.02 mn); revised statements were submitted afterwards. Separately, the Group states it is still reconciling taxable turnover, input tax eligible for credit and output tax payable per GST returns against the books.

Raw milk supply is a single-state exposure that is being diluted by intermediaries, not by geography: 94.51% of FY26 procurement came from Tamil Nadu (97.68% FY25, 99.62% FY24), while the share bought DIRECT from farmers fell from 96.61% (FY24) to 85.15% (FY25) to 74.34% (FY26), with third-party dairy operators rising from 9.25 mn to 45.61 mn to 101.67 mn litres. There are no formal supply arrangements with farmers and third-party operators supply on a purchase-order basis.

One plant, one region: all dairy and non-dairy lines, domestic and export, come out of the single Perundurai facility, which the RHP concedes may not be shiftable in a disruption; and 69.23% of FY26 revenue from operations came from South India (71.00% FY25, 73.68% FY24), with paneer, cheese and curd together 59.05% of FY26 revenue (62.63% and 66.16% in the two prior years).

The quality of the FY26 profit step deserves separation: total tax expense of Rs 314.81 mn on profit before tax of Rs 1,584.90 mn is struck after MAT credit of earlier years of Rs (245.61) mn and current-year MAT credit of Rs (59.56) mn, both first-time items; gross profit margin actually FELL to 32.97% from 33.89% in FY25 (31.21% FY24); and cash flow from operating activities declined to Rs 3,017.94 mn from Rs 3,148.57 mn even as profit rose 175.66%, against investing outflows of Rs 4,696.94 mn.

The EPCG position is large relative to the export book that must discharge it: aggregate outstanding export obligation under all active EPCG licences was Rs 10,028.13 mn as at March 31, 2026 (Rs 10,095.20 mn FY25; Rs 7,127.57 mn FY24) against FY26 export revenue of Rs 1,168.12 mn, only 3.72% of revenue from operations. The duty saved of Rs 1,948.71 mn is the bulk of contingent liabilities of Rs 2,290.09 mn as printed, itself 60.59% of net worth. This export obligation is disclosed SEPARATELY and is not part of the contingent liability total.

The food-safety record touches the flagship category: FSSAI proceedings at Ghaziabad on paneer samples alleged not to meet FPSFA specifications, with a Rs 0.20 mn penalty imposed by order dated February 5, 2025 and stayed by the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, Meerut, plus a second Ghaziabad hearing notice dated August 11, 2025; two further food-safety penalties paid (Rs 5,000, Tirunelveli, August 22, 2025; Rs 25,000, Bengaluru, November 14, 2025); a Legal Metrology panchnama and seizure at Vijayawada dated October 18, 2024 over an ice cream pack missing the month and year of manufacture; two TNPCB show cause notices dated December 31, 2024 and one KSPCB notice dated July 7, 2026.

Indirect tax disputes of Rs 313.91 mn are outstanding against the Company across three matters: a Rs 188.32 mn demand of December 31, 2023 under writ before the Madras High Court; a DGGI notice of December 6, 2024 seeking Rs 22.66 mn on 'parotta' and Rs 37.76 mn on 'tofu soya paneer' classification for 2020-21 to 2023-24; and a Tamil Nadu matter where the appellate order of April 30, 2026 left revised demands of Rs 44.05 mn and Rs 21.12 mn with further appeals to GSTAT in process. Five criminal complaints under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act for dishonoured distributor cheques have been filed BY the Company.

Senior-officer continuity is thin at exactly the roles that carry the reporting: Independent Director Subramaniam N resigned on July 6, 2026 having been appointed only on May 15, 2025; Company Secretary G Vivek resigned January 11, 2025; Chief Financial Officer Ramaswamy Subramanian resigned September 15, 2023 with the successor joining February 1, 2025. The RHP separately discloses that the majority of Directors are not and have not been on the board of any listed company, and that press reports carried past allegations of misconduct against the Whole-time Director and CEO in connection with his previous employment.

Control is near-absolute and the entry cost is asymmetric: Promoters hold 88.86% and the Promoter Group 93.00% pre-Offer, with post-Offer holding printed as [dot]; the Promoters' average cost of acquisition is Rs 0.06 per Equity Share against the Rs 139.76 Pre-IPO Placement price, following a 35:1 bonus issue of 612,500,000 Equity Shares on March 17, 2025 that took the count from 17,500,000 to 630,000,000 within 18 months of the Offer.

Related-party dependencies sit inside the operating chain: IT consultancy and software support from Magiva Technologies Private Limited, a Promoter Group entity, at Rs 19.65 / 18.00 / 16.75 mn plus vehicle maintenance of Rs 9.95 / 4.20 / 6.22 mn across FY26-FY24; Rs 88.60 mn paid to the Chairman and Managing Director in FY26 for assignment of a trademark; Rs 71.25 mn paid to the Promoters for the shares of Asal Food Products; and two chilling-centre premises leased from the Chairman and Managing Director for 34-year terms, within 21 of 29 chilling centres (72.41%) being on leased premises.

Working capital absorbed cash as the business scaled: net working capital rose Rs 2,454.59 mn (FY24) to Rs 2,699.39 mn (FY25) to Rs 4,109.80 mn (FY26) - working capital days 49, then 42, then back up to 48 - with trade receivables at Rs 1,765.07 mn from Rs 1,022.31 mn, an expected credit loss allowance of Rs 180.15 mn, gross receivables of Rs 553.1 lakhs sitting beyond three years, and inventory turnover days of 53 / 55 / 46.

The workforce shrank while the business grew: 1,694 employees (FY24) to 1,524 (FY25) to 1,317 (FY26), with 671, 547 and 398 resignations and attrition rates of 41.13%, 34.05% and 29.08%, unskilled attrition at 69.76% / 69.31% / 29.81%, alongside 3,224 contract labourers as of March 31, 2026 for whose wages the Company may be held responsible if contractors default.

A second, much larger project sits outside the Objects and outside this document's funding plan: a 1,94,866 sq m MIDC land parcel at Baramati allotted for Rs 490.65 mn under an agreement dated October 30, 2025, and an MoU dated January 13, 2026 with the Government of Maharashtra proposing investment of approximately Rs 11,300 mn with project commencement proposed in December 2029. Tamil Nadu MoUs of November 23, 2021 and January 8, 2024 (Rs 6,000 mn and Rs 5,000 mn) and a government order of August 20, 2024 carrying a Rs 12,770 mn capital commitment against a 1.75% turnover-based subsidy are also outstanding.

Gujarat Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation and Kaira District Cooperative Milk Producers Union have sued over trade dress on certain ice cream products and freezers, seeking permanent and mandatory injunctions and damages of Rs 20.10 mn; 16 trademark applications remain pending in India and two outside it, including three assigned from the Promoter and two from Briyas Foods where the change of proprietor is still pending.

Consent to operate under the Water Act and the Air Act for the Perundurai facility itself is an application acknowledged only on April 8, 2026 and still pending as at the RHP date, alongside a Karnataka fire NOC applied for on July 18, 2025 and Gundlupete chilling-centre consents still being applied for.

open_questions: Paneer utilisation fell to 52.44% in FY26 after capacity went from 72 to 192 MT per day, yet Rs 3,945.00 mn of Net Proceeds funds further new lines and cheddar capacity is being taken from 15.6 to 120 MT per day - what demand commitments or order visibility underpin the next tranche of capacity, and what utilisation is assumed in the ITCOT cost-benefit case?

Why did the direct-from-farmer share of procurement fall from 96.61% (FY24) to 74.34% (FY26) while third-party operator volume rose from 9.25 mn to 101.67 mn litres, and what does that shift do to procurement cost, traceability and the 'no middlemen' positioning that supports the Rs 77.79 per litre realisation?

Cash flow from operations fell to Rs 3,017.94 mn in FY26 from Rs 3,148.57 mn while profit rose 175.66% - what drove the divergence beyond the Rs 4,109.80 mn net working capital build, and what is the FY27 working capital plan once Rs 4,968.61 mn of borrowings is repaid from Net Proceeds?

What is the remediation timeline and independent verification for the CARO items that persist into FY2026 - the 3% of Company gross block and 21% of Subsidiary gross carrying value still unreconciled, the internal audit coverage gap, and the GST turnover and ITC reconciliation still described as in process?

How will the Rs 10,028.13 mn of outstanding EPCG export obligation at March 31, 2026 be discharged on an export book of Rs 1,168.12 mn a year, licence by licence, and what is the exposure if extensions are not granted - the RHP quantifies duty saved of Rs 1,948.71 mn but not interest and penalties?
Why did the Independent Director appointed on May 15, 2025 resign on July 6, 2026, and what were the circumstances of the CFO vacancy between September 15, 2023 and February 1, 2025?

The RHP prints two conflicting footnotes on where export sales sit in the channel table ('Our Business' page 229 places them in general trade, Risk Factor 42 on page 59 places them in 'Other channels') - which is correct, and does the general trade decline from 44.53% to 37.69% of revenue over FY24-FY26 hold on either basis?

What is the funding plan and board-approved timetable for the Baramati project (MIDC land at Rs 490.65 mn, MoU proposing approximately Rs 11,300 mn of investment with commencement proposed December 2029), given that none of it is an Object of this Offer and net worth stands at Rs 3,779.95 mn?

On what basis is the Company confident of manufacturing whey protein concentrate and lactose - products in which it states it has no prior manufacturing experience - to specification, and what is the offtake route for a 44 TPD lactose line given whey powder currently runs at 48.93% utilisation and is sold largely to one biscuit manufacturer?

What is the status of the second Ghaziabad FSSAI proceeding (hearing notice dated August 11, 2025, cross-examination sought October 31, 2025) and the appeal against the stayed Rs 0.20 mn penalty, both concerning paneer, the category that is 29.42% of revenue?

How many retail outlets actually hold the 15,062 visi coolers, 25,824 ice cream freezers and 573 chocolate coolers deployed as at March 31, 2026, and what incremental revenue per unit is assumed for the 66,000 further units costing Rs 1,553.13 mn - the printed outlet series (13,211, 4,065 and 10,503 for FY26, FY25 and FY24) cannot be a cumulative deployed base?
verdict.our_read: A single-plant Tamil Nadu value-added dairy company (FY26 revenue Rs 31,383.64 mn, +33.58%; PAT Rs 1,270.09 mn; net worth Rs 3,779.95 mn against borrowings of Rs 16,718.53 mn) whose thesis rides on filling capacity it already tripled - paneer utilisation fell to 52.44% in FY26.

EBITDA margin improved 12.21% to 13.21% to 13.87% and PAT margin 1.07% to 1.96% to 4.05%, but gross profit margin fell to 32.97% in FY26 from 33.89% in FY25, and the FY26 tax line carries first-time MAT credits of Rs 245.61 mn (earlier years) and Rs 59.56 mn (current year) within a total tax expense of Rs 314.81 mn on PBT of Rs 1,584.90 mn.

strengths_observed: Three-year compounding with operating leverage, verified in the certified KPI table: revenue from operations Rs 18,216.09 mn (FY24) to Rs 23,495.03 mn (FY25) to Rs 31,383.64 mn (FY26), the last step +33.58%; EBITDA Rs 2,223.30 / 3,103.46 / 4,352.19 mn at margins of 12.21% / 13.21% / 13.87%; PAT Rs 194.44 / 460.74 / 1,270.09 mn at margins of 1.07% / 1.96% / 4.05%. The MD&A attributes the 175.66% FY26 profit step to total expenses falling from 96.50% to 95.16% of revenue from operations and to recognition of previously unrecognised MAT credit of Rs 245.61 million.

Documented category positions rather than asserted ones, all for Fiscal 2026 (Source: 1Lattice Report, commissioned by the Company): approximately 19.0% of India's organised packaged paneer market by value (largest private brand); approximately 12% of the Southern region's organised cheese segment and approximately 5% nationally among private players (ranked third); approximately 13% of India's organised yogurt market and 35% to 40% of the organised Greek yogurt market; approximately 7% of South India's organised curd market. Paneer, the flagship, was Rs 9,231.71 mn / 29.42% of FY26 revenue from operations.

Pricing power is evidenced, not claimed: paneer and curd are typically priced 10% to 30% above the average market price of large Indian brands, and realisation per litre of milk procured rose Rs 65.93 (FY24) to Rs 74.16 (FY25) to Rs 77.79 (FY26), stated to be the highest among listed peers (Source: 1Lattice Report). Gross profit was Rs 5,684.99 / 7,961.86 / 10,347.22 mn across FY24-FY26.

Backward integration is physical and disintermediated: raw milk procured direct from 74,654 farmers (33,126 of them women) across 25 districts within a 400 km radius of the plant, with farmers paid directly every 7 to 10 days; 396.15 mn litres procured in FY26 against 307.20 mn (FY25) and 272.80 mn (FY24); 3,907 automated milk collection units and 29 chilling centres, with testing at 3, 21 and 31 parameters across the three tiers.

The newer categories are the ones compounding: yoghurt revenue Rs 496.39 mn (FY24) to Rs 966.97 mn (FY25) to Rs 1,944.92 mn (FY26), within which Greek yoghurt went Rs 58.41 / 262.04 / 881.61 mn and Skyr Rs 24.88 / 89.01 / 325.74 mn; ice cream Rs 345.15 / 1,376.78 / 2,110.86 mn from a Fiscal 2024 launch. 538 new SKUs and 5 new categories added between April 1, 2022 and March 31, 2026 contributed Rs 8,836.74 mn, 28.16% of FY26 revenue from operations.

Distribution and channel mix widened materially: distributors 2,558 (FY24) to 3,062 (FY25) to 4,001 (FY26) across 22 states and 5 union territories, more than 3,75,000 retail touchpoints, 57 C&F depots and 144 exclusive parlours as of the RHP date; revenue from online channels rose Rs 1,368.52 mn / 7.51% to Rs 4,299.59 mn / 13.70% of revenue from operations over the same three years.

Owned downstream logistics and energy: 63 milk tankers (average 23,150 litres), 282 reefer trucks (~10,485 kg payload) and 34 ambient trucks as of March 31, 2026, with 26 owned vehicles electric and IoT fleet tracking; 29 MW solar (Kavilipalayam, Chitode, Arasanur) and 2 MW wind (Kayathar) meeting approximately 75% of total energy requirement, with a further 10 MW under expansion, and all boiler operations on certified biofuels.

Debt-service metrics improved each year on the printed ratios: interest coverage 1.60 (FY24) to 2.02 (FY25) to 2.50 times (FY26); debt service coverage 1.04 / 1.16 / 1.63 times; net debt to EBITDA 4.59 / 4.37 / 3.81 times; debt to equity 3.68 / 4.20 / 3.61 times. The single largest Object, Rs 4,968.61 mn of borrowing repayment, is directed at this line, and Rs 1,443.39 mn of the Rs 6,412.00 mn total proposed to be repaid had already been repaid from Pre-IPO Placement proceeds as on June 30, 2026.

Institutional capital came in at a struck price shortly before the Offer: Jongsong Investments Pte. Ltd., an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Temasek Holdings, subscribed 543,789 Equity Shares and 25,000,000 CCPS at Rs 139.76 each aggregating Rs 3,570.00 mn on April 30, 2026 (CCPS converted July 22, 2026), holds 5.16% pre-Offer, and the Fresh Issue was consequently cut from Rs 17,850.00 mn to Rs 14,280.00 mn. None of the Promoters' Equity Shares are pledged.

The expansion needs no new site or land: every Object line item is inside the existing owned Perundurai facility, the RHP records that no land is to be acquired and that no licences or approvals are required at this stage because civil work had not commenced, and power is to come from existing TNPDCL arrangements plus the existing 29 MW solar and 2 MW wind capacity.
